basis: Craniosynostosis and pectoral/limb malformations define syndrome; strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Nail and hair morphology alone does not establish tissue damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: frequent nail and hair variants lack evidence of functional impairment or destructive skin disease.

basis: Skin aplasia/blistering, cleft palate and ectrodactyly define syndrome; persistent ptosis/ectropion constitute an additional defining eyelid constellation; frequency unknown.

decisions.ocular: involved: defining ptosis/ectropion; three primary slots occupied by core skin-palate-limb abnormalities. [MeSH](https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=C535885).
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: ectrodactyly and phalangeal hypoplasia are core congenital skeletal malformations.

basis: Neurologic and retinal damage each inferred in >=30% across major forms; pooled frequency uncertain. [CDG network](https://fcdgc.rarediseasesnetwork.org/diseases-studied/dhdds-cdg).

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal degeneration defines the recessive form; 30-40 reported families versus 59 dominant neurologic cases suggests >=30% across this umbrella, with ascertainment uncertainty.

basis: Defining skeletal/cardiac syndrome; dental malocclusion 5/10 and conductive hearing loss 4/11 support involvement. Separately diagnosed sleep apnea excluded.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac anomalies are an explicitly named defining component, although variably expressed; arrhythmia occurs in 3/9 and structural heart defects are documented.

basis: Ischemic necrosis directly damages hepatic parenchyma; a vascular cause or classification does not establish direct vessel damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hepatic infarction specifies liver necrosis, without necessarily specifying thrombosis or another intrinsic vessel lesion.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; encephalopathy 6/6 and dystonia 5/5 establish neurologic damage. Cardiomyopathy 1/6 is below threshold; optic atrophy frequency unknown.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy occurs in 6/6, with dystonia and CNS injury; these are consequences of the defining mitochondrial metabolic defect.

basis: Deep soft-tissue sarcoma; lung metastases directly occupy lung in ~37-39% in a 59-patient cohort. [Cohort](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7308468/).

decisions.pulmonary: involved: lung metastases occurred in approximately 22-23/59 patients (~37-39%); direct metastatic occupation exceeds the threshold over the disease course.

basis: Carpotarsal osteolysis and nephropathy define syndrome; renal insufficiency 15/19. Corneal opacity 3/9 (~33%) supports ocular involvement, with small-sample uncertainty.

decisions.renal: primary: nephropathy is explicitly named and included in the disease definition; renal insufficiency in 15/19 confirms it is a central manifestation despite variable expression.

basis: Autistic neurodevelopmental impairment and a persistent facial cutaneous capillary malformation define the syndrome.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the defining port-wine angioma is a structural capillary malformation; capillaries belong to the cardiovascular axis.

basis: CNS hypomyelination defines disease; optic atrophy 2/6 (~33%) supports ocular damage. Contractures 2/6 reflect secondary effects of spasticity rather than direct skeletal disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint contractures in 2/6 exceed the frequency threshold but arise secondarily from neurologic spasticity; direct musculoskeletal disease is not established.
